Complete models, each on a page of its own with the same parts: what the model is and why a modeler would build it this way, its state-transition diagram, its parameters, the code, a result with a plot, and where to go next. Each page runs as it is, in a few seconds. They cover a range of diseases and structures, rather than building one model up step by step as the [tutorials](tutorials.qmd) do.

## Models

| Model | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [SIR, four ways](gallery/sir.qmd) | The four ways of writing a model, which give the same model; the same model as an ODE, two kinds of stochastic model, and agents |
| [Checks against theory](gallery/theory_checks.qmd) | The final size against the Kermack–McKendrick equation, as an ODE; the chance of a major outbreak against 1 − 1/R0, with many stochastic runs |
| [SEIR with a realistic infectious period](gallery/seir_erlang.qmd) | A latent period; an infectious period with Erlang stages against an exponential one |
| [Hospitalization and death](gallery/hospitalization.qmd) | A split on entry (who goes to hospital) and competing hazards (death or discharge); severity by age as a Python function, run as compartments and as agents |
| [Cholera with a water reservoir](gallery/cholera.qmd) | A state that is not people (bacteria in the water), with flows in from and out to outside the model |
| [Age groups and contacts](gallery/age_contacts.qmd) | An age-stratified SIR with a contact matrix; the United Kingdom's population with contacts by setting, and a school closure that removes one setting |
| [Vaccination as a stratification](gallery/vaccination_strata.qmd) | Vaccinated and unvaccinated groups, and a campaign that moves people between them |
| [Cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, fitted to data](gallery/outcomes_fit.qmd) | Outcomes with delays; data made from the model; fitting β with `sim.fit()` |
| [An STI on a sexual network](gallery/sexual_network.qmd) | Transmission per sex act over partnerships; many runs as agents |
| [Measles in London, two ways](gallery/measles_london.qmd) | He et al. (2010)'s stochastic measles model with school terms and cohort entry: declared with a little code, and as code; fitted with a likelihood of its own, compiled, and with a particle filter |
| [Beyond disease](gallery/beyond_disease.qmd) | Agent-based models with no disease: wealth that becomes unequal, and birds that flock, each as a module written as code |

## Models from other frameworks

Each framework that Starsim can [import from](user_guide/building_import.qmd) has a page in the [Lingua Franca](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/) docs, starting with a showcase model written in that framework and in Starsim, with how their results agree and how long each takes:

| Framework | Model |
|---|---|
| [Atomica](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/atomica/#the-same-model-in-both) | Atomica's SIR demo, from its framework workbook and databook |
| [camdl](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/camdl/#the-same-model-in-both) | A closed SIR, observed through weekly reported cases |
| [EMULSION](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/emulsion/#the-same-model-in-both) | EMULSION's compartmental SIR |
| [EpiModel](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/epimodel/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SIS over partnerships that form and dissolve |
| [epipack](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/epipack/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SIRS written as reaction processes |
| [epydemix](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/epydemix/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SIR in Kenya's population, with contact matrices between five age groups |
| [epymorph](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/epymorph/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SIRS in three places, with commuting between them |
| [flepiMoP](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/flepimop/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SEIR in two provinces whose residents commute between them |
| [LASER](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/laser/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SEIR in a city and fifteen smaller places, coupled by gravity |
| [MEmilio](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/memilio/#the-same-model-in-both) | An age-resolved SECIR with seasonality and a cut in contacts |
| [NumPy](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/numpy/#the-same-model-in-both) | A stochastic SEIR in daily steps for a million people |
| [odin](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/odin/#the-same-model-in-both) | A discrete-time stochastic SEIR in four age groups, with seasonal forcing |
| [SimInf](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/siminf/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SIR in each of 1,600 cattle herds, linked by movements |
| [summer2](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/summer2/#the-same-model-in-both) | An SIR with deaths, stratified by age and by location, with a mixing matrix for each |

## Library modules

Starsim also comes with a library of example modules, which are illustrative rather than validated: their parameter values are indicative, and some are placeholders. Use them as starting points to copy and adapt. They are imported with `import starsim.library as ssl`:

- **Diseases** (`ssl.diseases`): HIV with CD4 counts (with `ssl.diseases.ART` for treatment), cholera with an environmental reservoir, Ebola with transmission from unburied bodies, measles as an SEIR, a non-communicable disease, and simple models of malaria, TB, COVID, influenza, RSV, pertussis, dengue, typhoid, polio, syphilis, and gonorrhea.
- **Networks** (`ssl.networks`): households from survey data, people who move in space and connect to those nearby (`DiskNet`), and theoretical networks such as Erdős–Rényi.
- **Maternal, newborn, and child health** (`ssl.mnch`): fetal health, neonatal sepsis, and congenital disease.
- **Health economics** (`ssl.econ`): costs, disability-adjusted life years, discounting, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios.

[Library](user_guide/library_index.qmd) in the user guide describes them, and how to use them.

## Scripts in the repository

A few longer examples are kept as scripts in the [`docs/examples`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/tree/main/docs/examples) folder of the repository, to read and adapt:

- **An embedding network** ([`networks/embedding.py`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/blob/main/docs/examples/networks/embedding.py)): pairs people by their closeness in a continuous space of traits.
- **One model in several languages** ([`translations/`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/tree/main/docs/examples/translations)): the same simple SIS model written in plain Python, Numba, JAX, Julia, and Rust, next to the Starsim version, for comparing their speed.
- **LASER** ([`laser/`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/tree/main/docs/examples/laser)): a LASER example and its Starsim equivalents, with scripts to time them.
